area.title: Roles and addresses page and the party pickers
area.scope: The consignment addresses (roles and addresses) page and the five party pickers: which roles show for which commodity, role hints, the add links, the same-as shortcuts, the picker search, list, pagination, view details and selection, which addresses a picker offers, saving a pick, and the animals frontend's read of the address book. Stops at adding a new address from the journey and editing a copied address (party-address-add-and-edit), and at the CPH number, permanent address and contact address (cph-permanent-and-contact). Includes the high-risk plants frontend's place of destination and consignor pickers, its shared address-book picker helpers, its identification numbers page and party reference handling.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

claims.statement: Picker paging is a plain link, not a form submit, and each page link carries the search term (q), the page number (page) and the currently ticked address (selected) in its query string, so a row ticked on one page is not lost on paging.

Paging is a link, not a submit, so everything the next page needs travels
 * in the query string: the search term, the page and the row the trader has
 * already ticked. Without the selection a trader who picks a row on page one
 * and then pages loses it.

claims.statement: Dropping a dangling reference happens only for the current request; the stored answer is left until the next save rebuilds from the current answers, and the stored answers are kept so a page can tell 'answered, then deleted' from 'never answered'.

Request-local. What was saved is left alone in the store — the next commit
 * that rebuilds from the current answers is what persists the clear — and the
 * engine keeps the stored answers beside the sanitised ones so a page can still
 * tell "answered, then deleted" from "never answered".

claims.quote: Select Newer Than Target 1791394803707 4 ... Select Newer Than Target 1791394803707 0 ... Select Paged Consignor 1791394803707
claims.note: Page 2 opens with the record page 1 closed on (Newer Than Target 0), because another worker added a record between the two loads; the book is shared across tests.

claims.statement: After the INS add handshake, the newly created address appears first on page one of the picker.
claims.quote: Showing 5 of 28 addresses ... Select Handshake Farm 1791394803511

claims.statement: When the results run past one page, the picker shows GOV.UK pagination: numbered page links with an ellipsis for skipped pages, the current page marked with aria-current, and a Next link.
claims.quote:
... aria-label="Page 1" aria-current="page"> 1 ... aria-label="Page 2"> 2
  • ⋯
    • ... aria-label="Page 6"> 6 ... rel="next"> Next page

claims.statement: On page 2 the pagination shows Previous, pages 1, 2 (current) and 3, an ellipsis, page 6 and Next.
claims.quote: rel="prev"> Previous page ... aria-label="Page 1"> 1 ... aria-label="Page 2" aria-current="page"> 2 ... aria-label="Page 3"> 3 ... govuk-pagination__item--ellipsis"> ⋯ ... aria-label="Page 6"> 6 ... rel="next"> ... Next

claims.statement: Pagination links are plain GET links to the picker URL with ?page=N, so paging works without JavaScript and loads a fresh page.
claims.ref: trace 98845 request GET /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-ZAQEWW/consignors/select?page=2 (200), step pw:api@101 click Next
claims.quote: href="/live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-ZAQEWW/consignors/select?page=2" rel="next"

claims.statement: A page other than the first carries its number in the form's hidden page field.
claims.quote: <INPUT __playwright_value_="2" type="hidden" name="page" value="2"></INPUT>

claims.statement: Searching is a server round trip over the whole address book: a search for a name returns only the matching records, here 'Tech Imports Ltd' narrowed to one row.
claims.ref: trace 98845 call@125, steps pw:api@84 fill 'Tech Imports Ltd' and pw:api@85 click Search
claims.quote: <INPUT __playwright_value_="Tech Imports Ltd" ... id="q" name="q" type="text" value="Tech Imports Ltd" ...> ... Showing 1 of 1 addresses

claims.statement: A search matches part of a name: 'Kolding1791394803707' found both 'Danish Meat Export Kolding1791394803707' and 'Jutland Swine Kolding1791394803707'.
claims.ref: trace 98845 call@137, assertions expect@92 'Showing 2 of 2 addresses' and expect@93 radio 'Select Jutland Swine Kolding1791394803707' passed
claims.quote: Showing 2 of 2 addresses ... Select Jutland Swine Kolding1791394803707 ... Select Danish Meat Export Kolding1791394803707

claims.statement: When the search results fit on one page the pagination block is not shown.
claims.ref: trace 98845 call@137; assertion expect@94 toHaveCount(0) on link 'Page 2' passed
claims.quote: Expect "toHaveCount" getByRole('link', { name: 'Page 2' })

claims.statement: The search term stays in the Search field after the results load.
claims.quote: <INPUT __playwright_value_="Kolding1791394803707" class="govuk-input govuk-!-width-two-thirds" id="q" name="q" type="text" value="Kolding1791394803707" aria-describedby="q-hint"></INPUT>

claims.statement: Searching with an empty field restores the whole address book and its pagination.
